title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
prompt: Given an integer array `nums`, return the maximum result of `nums[i] XOR nums[j]`, where `0 <= i, j < nums.length` (i and j may be equal only if that doesn't matter for the maximum, though in practice the best pair is always distinct indices since `x XOR x = 0`).

examples.explanation: Some pair in the array XORs to 127.

hints: Trying every pair is O(n^2), which is too slow at the given size; you need to find, for each number, its best XOR partner faster than by brute force.
Think of each number as a fixed-length binary string (say 32 bits) and insert all of them into a binary trie, where each node has at most two children: 0 and 1.

For each number, walk the trie bit by bit from the most significant bit, greedily choosing the child representing the OPPOSITE bit whenever it exists — that greedy choice is always safe because a higher bit set to 1 in the XOR result dominates any combination of lower bits.

solution.approach: Insert every number into a binary trie, processing each number's bits from most significant (bit 31) to least significant, so shared high-order bits share trie paths. Then for each number, greedily walk the trie trying, at each bit, to go to the child representing the opposite bit of the current number — since a 1 in a higher XOR bit position is worth more than any combination of all lower bits combined, greedily maximizing from the top down is always optimal. If the opposite-bit child doesn't exist, fall back to the same-bit child. Track the best XOR value found across all numbers.
